newsitem.title: CHINA: France's Chirac avoids issue of arms sales to China.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac avoids issue of arms sales to China.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac on Friday brushed aside suggestions that Paris would break with its Western allies and resume arms sales to China.
But he stressed that France would abide by its 1994 pledge to China not to sell weapons to Beijing's island arch-rival, Taiwan.
Asked whether France would restart arms sales to Beijing, Chirac told reporters: "This is not a topical question."
He declined to comment further on suggestions in the French media that Paris is seeking to restart sales to the lucrative Chinese market.
Sales have been frozen by the European Union (EU) since Beijing's bloody 1989 military crackdown on student-led pro-democracy demonstrations.
French Defence Minister Charles Millon said last month that he hoped the EU ban on arms sales to China could be lifted in future.
China is eager to modernise its large but technologically lagging armed forces with advanced weaponry from the West.
Taiwan is also looking to buy more sophisticated arms to keep pace with rival China, but Chirac made it clear that the island would have to look elsewhere.
France would "abide to the letter" of its agreement with Beijing barring arms sales to Taipei, he said.
Sino-French relations soured in the early 1990s over France's sales of frigates and 60 Mirage jet fighters to Taiwan, which Beijing considers a rebel province.
They have gradually recovered since Paris pledged to end arms sales to the island.
Beijing has vowed to recover Taiwan and has threatened to use force if the island declared independence.
In March last year, Beijing held missile tests and war games near Taiwan in a show of force ahead of the island's first direct presidential elections.
